Author: Dinesh Mehta

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature For Rajasthan At Jodhpur

sentences.text:
Ramprakash Bhutra S/o Pukhraj Bhutra, Aged About 62 Years, By Caste Maheshwari,
(Seller And Owner) M/s Maheshwari Trading Company, Main Market, Raipur, District Pali
(Rajasthan).

----Petitioner Versus
1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Food Safety Commissioner, Rajasthan, Jaipur.

2. Anand Kumar, Food Safety Officer, Office Of Chief Medical And Health Officer, Pali (Raj.).
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. D.D. Chitlangi Justice Dinesh Mehta Order
02/08/2019

The present writ petition is directed against the order dated 26.04.2019, passed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Jaipur in an appeal, filed by the petitioner against the order dated 06.11.2017, passed by the Prescribed Authority and Additional District Magistrate, Pali.
The facts in brief, are that the petitioner Proprietor of M/s. Maheshwari Trading Company deals in oil and other miscellaneous provisions.
In pursuance of a survey, conducted at his shop on 20.07.2015, a sample of groundnut oil was drawn by respondent No.2, which was found to be substandard.

The petitioner himself moved an application under Section 26(2)(2) of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2006') for compounding, for (2 of 3)
[CW-11419/2019] which a penalty to the tune of Rs.1,50,000/- under Section 52 of the Act of 2006 was imposed upon him, by order dated 06.11.2017 by the Prescribed Authority.

The petitioner preferred an appeal against the said order, before the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal,
Jaipur, which has been rejected by the Tribunal, vide its order dated 26.04.2019.

Impugning the order dated 06.11.2017 and 26.04.2019, learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that the prescribed authority has erred in imposing a penalty and the appellate authority in upholding, the fine of Rs.1,50,000/-, without taking into account the relevant facts and factors, such as petitioner was simply a seller and not manufacturer and that it was the first case against him.
I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the material available on record.

sentences.text: Concededly, the petitioner himself had moved the application for composition of offence, for which the competent authority, instead of launching appropriate proceedings and probing further or conducting further enquiry, decided to impose a fine of Rs.1,50,000/- under Section 52(1) of the the Act of 2006, for the admitted breach of provisions contained in Section 26(2) (2) of the Act of 2006.
Neither before the authority concerned nor before the Appellate Authority, the petitioner has pointed as to how determination of penalty of Rs.1,50,000/- was erroneous.

Mr. Chitlangi, learned counsel for the petitioner, however, invited attention of the Court towards invoice of M/s. Ghisulal Udhyog, the manufacturer of the concerned groundnut oil (3 of 3)
[CW-11419/2019] and prayed that the penalty, as a matter of fact, ought to have been imposed upon the manufacturer.
Firstly, it is to be noted that the invoice, which has been placed before this Court, has not been placed before the authorities below and hence, the same cannot be considered.
That apart, the provisions of the Act of 2006, makes the seller as well as the manufacturer liable for penalty and prosecution.

The petitioner, being a seller of the substandard goods, is equally responsible and thus,
no illegality or irregularity can be found in the orders impugned.
I find no force in the writ petition, for which it is dismissed.
The Stay Application No.11356/2019 also stands dismissed accordingly.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 18-skm/-
